audit.why: MIRROR CHECK against audits/top/zac__sejuani.json: his page reads Zac 4 / Skill 3 / Sejuani 0 and this page reads Skill / Zac / Zac / Skill / Skill / Zac / Zac — the same four-three-zero split, stage for stage. The two directions already agree and neither needs moving. It also matches the record: 49.23% over 65 games here against 59.76% over 82 on his side, i.e. a lane Zac edges without ever owning outright.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike recommends Sunfire Aegis or Heartsteel. Unstable Matter deals a percentage of the target's maximum health, every 5 seconds, and Cell Division heals him — neither fact appears in either layer, and Grievous Wounds is never mentioned.
audit.why: Heartsteel is the single worst first item against a champion whose W is percent-max-health magic damage on a 5-second cooldown, so the entry's item advice makes its own stated problem worse. And the thing the spike is actually trying to solve — 'his passive healing loop' — is answered by anti-heal, not by burn: Sunfire's tick does not stop blob reabsorption, Grievous Wounds does.
audit.corrected: Unstable Matter: percent of your maximum health, 5s flat. Skip Heartsteel and take Grievous Wounds against Cell Division's healing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (Unstable Matter cd 5, 'deals a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage', percentHealth; Cell Division heal flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: Fury of the North's Frost Armor grants immunity to slows, and Zac's only two slows are Stretching Strikes and Let's Bounce!. Neither layer mentions it.
audit.why: MIRROR REUSE — this is the top finding in the already-published zac__sejuani.json audit, stated here from Sejuani's side so the two pages agree. Every approach in this lane starts with a Sejuani who has been farming out of combat, so Frost Armor is up and the first Q slow simply does not hold her. The buff is therefore a window: step up on it, and his kite pattern does not start working until his damage has stripped it. Nothing on this page tells the player that the buff they already have is the reason the step-up is free.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor makes you immune to slows out of combat — his Stretching Strikes and Let's Bounce! slows do nothing until his damage strips the buff, so the first step-up is free.
sources: audits/top/zac__sejuani.json (mirror audit, point 4: Frost Armor slow immunity vs Zac's Q and R slows)
champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (Fury of the North: 'immunity to slows')
champ-data/_kits/zac.json (slow flags on Q and R only)

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer calls Stretching Strikes a bounce twice: 'before his Q lets him bounce away' and 'Zac gets his Q bounce too'. Stretching Strikes is an 800-unit ranged grab that pulls the target, knocks up and slows — it is not mobility and it moves you, not him.
audit.why: The error inverts who controls the distance. A player told Zac's Q is an escape holds his own Arctic Assault back waiting for a disengage that never comes; in reality the Q reaches 800 units, more than Arctic Assault's 650, and is the tool that drags Sejuani into Unstable Matter range. It is also an auto-attack reset, so the tell is the attack wind-up rather than the cast — the same read the entry already teaches for other matchups and omits here.
audit.corrected: Stretching Strikes is an 800-unit grab that pulls you toward him, knocks up and slows, on 14/12.5/11/9.5/8s. It is an auto-reset — watch the wind-up, not the cast.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (Stretching Strikes: range 800, cd 14/12.5/11/9.5/8, 'stretches an arm, grabbing an enemy', knockup, slow, autoReset)

audit.whatIsWrong: Cell Division revives Zac. Upon taking fatal damage he splits into four bloblets and comes back if any survive, on a 5-minute cooldown. The entry refers to 'passive blobs' and 'blob pickups' four times and only ever describes the healing half.
audit.why: It changes the value of every ultimate Sejuani spends on him. The late paragraph's whole plan is 'whichever of you lands a multi-man R at the right objective' wins — but if Zac stands back up thirty seconds into that fight, a 120-second Glacial Prison bought a delay rather than a kill. The correct habit is to check whether Cell Division is available before committing R on him specifically, and to kill the bloblets when it triggers; neither is stated anywhere.
audit.corrected: Cell Division also revives him — fatal damage splits him into four bloblets and he returns if any live, on a 5-minute cooldown. Kill the blobs, and check it before you spend R on him.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (Cell Division: 'Upon taking fatal damage, Zac splits into 4 bloblets ... he will revive ... This ability has a 5 minute cooldown')

audit.whatIsWrong: Elastic Slingshot is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in both layers and its duration is never given.
audit.why: The instruction is 'step up only on its downtime' and 'never step into the river bush without tracking that cooldown first', which needs the number the page does not have. Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9 — a 21-second window at rank 1 that shrinks to 9, so the early game gives a far bigger punish window than the mid game and the entry never signals that change.
audit.corrected: Elastic Slingshot: 21/18/15/12/9s. Let's Bounce!: 120/105/90s. Unstable Matter: 5s flat.

edits.after: Q into double W-sweep into Permafrost is your first combo window — punish his blob pickup, and note Frost Armor makes you immune to the Stretching Strikes slow.

notes: MIRROR: audits/top/zac__sejuani.json already exists and I reused its findings rather than re-deriving them. Its level chart (Zac 4 / Skill 3 / Sejuani 0) matches this page stage for stage, so the two directions agree and I changed nothing there. I have restated its headline finding — Frost Armor's slow immunity against Zac's only two slows, Stretching Strikes and Let's Bounce! — from Sejuani's side, where it reads as a window rather than a warning: the first step-up out of combat is free because his slow does not hold. Best new find on this side: the content layer calls Stretching Strikes a bounce twice, 'before his Q lets him bounce away' and 'Zac gets his Q bounce too'. It is an 800-unit ranged grab that pulls you toward him — longer than Arctic Assault's 650 — so the entry has the direction of the ability backwards, and a player waiting for Zac to disengage with it is instead getting dragged into Unstable Matter range. Second: Unstable Matter is percent-max-health magic damage on 5 seconds flat, and the first-item spike recommends Heartsteel, which is the one purchase that makes it hit harder; the W is not mentioned anywhere in either layer. Third: Cell Division revives him after fatal damage on a 5-minute cooldown, and the entry describes only its healing half across four separate mentions — which matters because the late paragraph's win condition is landing a multi-man R at an objective, and a revive converts a 120-second ultimate from a kill into a delay. Fourth: Elastic Slingshot is the named matchup-defining cooldown in both layers and its 21/18/15/12/9s value appears nowhere. NOT ASSERTED: the kit file carries a 'grounding' flag on Elastic Slingshot, but Riot's own description of the ability says nothing about grounding, so per the flag-versus-description rule I did not use it anywhere. The six suspectNames hits on this matchup are all FALSE POSITIVES — 'Elastic Slingshot', 'Glacial Prison' and "Let's Bounce" are the correct names and the detector matched leading words and the missing exclamation mark.
